payload.body:
You can succeed in a visible role and still realize that you do not want to keep building your life around it. People notice what you can do, start relying on you for it, and keep giving you more of the same because your competence makes the next step look obvious from the outside.

Recognition can make the mismatch harder to admit. You keep proving yourself in the subject, position, responsibility, or public role that gets the strongest response even after you have started wanting something different. Being good at something and wanting to build your life around it are different questions.

Look at what success keeps asking you to repeat. More responsibility may give you more authority and make the role worth growing into. More recognition may simply make it harder to disappoint people who have already decided what you should be known for.

Being good at the role does not mean the role still fits you. The right direction gives your ability somewhere you still want to go. What you are building matters more than how impressive the role looks from the outside.
